master: Six original transparent 1672 × 941 ImageGen generations are packed into five 1528 × 941 runtime atlases. Each middle/near pair combines its landscape, architecture, exposed ground and water into a single painting. The camera uses two slices from each chapter and one strip from the shared four-row foreground atlas.
slices: A 144-pixel horizontal overlap was joined along a minimum-error pixel seam, maintaining natural orientation across repeats. The center and near banks do not mirror their buildings. MoonlitCamera.cs specifies row boundaries in source pixels. Test-LandscapeContact.ps1 checks the same rows and periodic horizontal adjacency as the player.

bambooNearReplacement.destination: Lower strip of Embankment2.png, under the original middle-distance bamboo wood
bambooNearReplacement.prompt: A single extra-wide 16:9 transparent PNG sprite for a premium pixel-art side-scrolling adventure, ONE EXTREMELY LOW, uninterrupted slice across the whole width of a mossy Vietnamese bamboo-forest floor, no buildings, no tree trunks, NO tall bamboo culms or poles. Detailed painterly faceted low-poly volumes translated into retro clustered pixels. Creeping ferns, shallow roots anchored visibly in eroded earth, soft micro-flowers, fallen bamboo leaves, smooth damp basalt stones, one inconspicuous mossy stone step breaking the bank. Shallow, asymmetrical top profile rises only with clumps of very short plants and low stones. Moonlight in jade accent on blue-violet natural rock shadows, limited crisp light edges, quiet dim green earth. Entire land strip drawn at the VERY BOTTOM of the canvas, top 55 percent transparent throughout, earth runs off left/right and bottom edges. Surface continuous enough to tile, on BOTH left and right edges and nearby, terrain has roughly SAME height and modest plain moss without any tall or cropped plants. All plants have full silhouettes, including frond tips. Width spans edge-to-edge with a fully opaque soil base along every pixel of bottom row, no isolated props, no isolated islands, no transparent holes in soil. All painted objects belong to the same continuous natural landform. No sky, moon, mist background, characters, lettering, framing or diagrams.

images.prompt:
A production game environment sprite atlas PNG on actual TRANSPARENT BACKGROUND, wide 16:9 canvas, 2 independent horizontally continuous side-scrolling parallax environment strips laid out in two rows. No lettering. Hand-crafted lush painterly pixel art with believable 3D volumes reduced to precise facets and pixel clusters, atmospheric cinematic low night light, slight top view of the terrain in a side scrolling game. Each strip must fill FULL WIDTH from the LEFT BORDER to the RIGHT BORDER, visible cut at both sides for mirrored tiling. TOP half is a MIDDLE DISTANCE panorama, BOTTOM half is a MUCH CLOSER foreground riverbank or slope without buildings. Within each HALF of image, upper part is transparent sky with irregular silhouette, lower part is one solid continuous strip of textured earth joined to all trees and objects. TOP strip fully confined to the top 48 percent, its dark cutaway base is a clean straight horizontal line at 46 percent of canvas height. Wide transparent gap across WHOLE picture from 47 to 53 percent of canvas height. Lower strip sits at bottom edge, all foliage and rocks between 55 percent height and 100 percent. Draw visible top planes, receding ground, worn stone retaining walls, crevices and roots, believable weight and contact shadows beneath whole groups. Grounded large cohesive place; understated detail in low-key jade and deep blue shadows, restrained moonlit rim highlights. No foreground character, no coins, no collectible, no cutout single objects, no stand-alone island, no isolated floating object, no sky gradient. Composition must be broad, flatter and continuous at both left/right edges, never a single rock or floating island centered with empty margins. TOP strip landmarks can be on the left 30% and rightmost 15% with mostly open low land in the middle. Lower strip: broad asymmetric shallow slope with unified plant masses and dark indigo soil beneath all plants across the entire width. Wide aspect ratio 16:9.
North Vietnamese village: TOP strip of continuous indigo, mossy brown terraced paddy embankment, wide old temple yard with modest wood communal đình hall and tiled roof, granite stone stairs meeting the courtyard ground, low retaining walls, bamboo fence, two trees rooted in rich soil; tiny informal vermilion lamp in rear eave. BOTTOM strip is near wet paddy bank, rows of rice seedlings plant into the earth, an old worn step at land-to-water transition and some reeds, moss-lipped eroded earth. Dusk blue and copper browns. Do not paint any extra roof on the lower strip.

A professional pixel-art sprite atlas, 16:9 frame, transparent background. FOUR very wide short separate horizontal strips, four rows of equal height. This is near camera scenic framing for a 2D Vietnamese folk-tale sidescroller. Each strip runs completely off both LEFT and RIGHT borders, a gently undulating extremely low silhouette. Every row has a few silhouettes of grasses, stones or plants on top and continuous dark indigo soil or wet stone beneath them, going all the way to a straight flat lower edge. The four strips are visually distinct and completely separated by slim empty transparent horizontal gutters. First row 0–23% height: dark near-camera rice paddy bund, a clump of rice and grass, deep navy earth, tiny dew rim details. Second row 25–48%: lush low ferns and bamboo leaves visibly rooted in an earthen bank, cool emerald rim light. Third row 50–73%: low muddy river edge with a few reed stems, pebbles, smooth meandering wet shore glints, deep violet indigo. Fourth row 75–100%: an old twisted horizontal banyan root crawling along the soil surface between dark rocks and moss, warm purple rim light. Hand crafted painterly pixel art, crisp faceted clusters read as simplified three-dimensional forms, deep nocturnal hues and strong silhouette, very restrained highlights. No trees, no text, no stage diagram, no frames, no watermarks, no floating elements. Each strip should be mostly land, low and continuous, edge to edge. Actual transparent gaps on all four strips above their greenery: no sky, no large scenery, no background. Visual hierarchy at a glance, beautiful varied asymmetrical patches surrounded by subdued breathing room.

preparation: FernShelf replaces rows 502–940 of the second atlas. Each 1672-pixel source is made periodic by a 144-pixel minimum-error overlap. A top-to-bottom path minimizing premultiplied RGBA difference chooses where left and right panorama edges join. Original vertical indices, painted perspective and contact shadows are preserved. The atmospheric horizon uses the existing Scenery1–4 plates; camera layer widths, vertical height and four scroll rates are in MoonlitCamera.cs.
